title: Flush Only When Full
prompt: ISO C design of stdio's rule. Given `struct bw { char buf[64]; size_t n; int flushes; };` (zero-initialized before use), implement `void bw_write(struct bw *w, const char *s, size_t len)` — append bytes; the moment one more byte would exceed 64, flush first (flushes++, n=0) and continue. Implement `size_t bw_pending(const struct bw *w)` returning w->n. NULL guards: w or s NULL with len>0 does nothing.

tests.name: fill exactly then overflow
tests.hint: 128 bytes fill the 64-buffer exactly once and overflow once: 1 flush, 64 pending. One more byte forces the second flush.

tests.name: single small write stays
tests.hint: Nothing overflows: zero flushes — buffering is the whole point.

tests.name: NULL guards
tests.hint: NULL inputs must change nothing — refuse by ignoring, not by crashing.
